newsitem.title: USA: Lenco Co of Nebraska files Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Lenco Co of Nebraska files Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

text.p: Lenco Co of Waverly, Nebraska today filed for Chapter 11 protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware.
In court papers, the company listed assets of $19.8 million and liabilities of $32.6, of which $9.7 million represented fixed liquidated unsecured debt.
Lenco's business is tool and die design, plastic injection molding and audio cassette assembly.
Among the 20 largest unsecured creditors is Marlborough Capital Investment Funds of Boston, with $6 million in subordinated notes.
Lenco Holdings Inc is listed as the owner of 20 percent or more of Lenco, according to court papers.
Lenco Chief Operating Officer Tony Natale told Reuters that although the company performed well operationally, it was overleveraged.
However Natale, a turnaround specialist brought in last month, said the company expects to emerge from Chapter 11 protection within 90 days.

"We've got general agreement with our top creditor, Finova Capital Corp, on an agreement to sell the company to a strategic buyer in the cassette and custom molding business who signed an asset purchase agreement, and we have adequate bridge and exit financing in place."

Lenco makes cassette blanks and sells them to music and spoken word houses which then add recorded tape. According to Natale, the company's 190 employees will not be affected by the bankruptcy and sale of assets. ""We intend to keep the operations going and have already received vendor support and don't expect any interruption in sales," Natale said.
